chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about a man who had an Umm al-Walad (concubine who bore him a child), so he married her to a man, and she bore him a boy. Then the man died, so she returned to her master. Is it for him to have intercourse with her? He said: She observes the waiting period from the husband, four months and ten days, then he has intercourse with her by ownership, without a new marriage contract.

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: Concubine who bore her master a child

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period and marital status of an Umm al-Walad after her husband dies?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the unique status of an Umm al-Walad married by her master, distinguishing her waiting period from that of a free wife. It establishes that upon completion of the Iddah, the master regains the right to consummate the relationship through simple ownership (Milk al-Yamin) rather than a new marriage contract, reflecting the juristic principle that her marriage was an extension of his dominion. This highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the legal mechanisms of concubinage and emancipation within the household structure.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Mahboub, from Wahab Bin Abd Rabbihi, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who had a mother of his child for him, so he married her to a man, so she gave birth to a boy. Then the man died. So she returned to her master. Is it for him that he copulates with her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She would observe the waiting period from the husband, of four months and ten days, then he can copulate with her by the ownership, without a marriage’.
